solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Large plant contained in small harbour (8)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A big plant sits inside a little harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contained in' looks like a container instruction, but 'contained' is simply a past-tense verb, placed in sequence.
annotation.definitionFit: The shaddock, or pomelo, is a citrus tree with the biggest fruit of its family, so 'large plant' is a description rather than a synonym.

entries.clue: Leading pair from Cumbria said goodbye (3,3)

indicatorNotes.Leading pair from: the pair leading a word are the two letters at its front
indicatorNotes.said: something said is heard rather than read, so the letters count by their sound

blocks.note: the first two letters of Cumbria, read out as letter names

annotation.surface: Two people from Cumbria take their leave.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is saying letters by their names: C is 'see' and U is 'you', which together make the everyday farewell.
annotation.definitionFit: A casual spoken farewell, used where 'goodbye' would be formal.

entries.clue: A short notice this writer placed around wreath (6)

indicatorNotes.short: a short form of a word is its abbreviation, so advertisement becomes AD
indicatorNotes.placed around: something placed around is turned about, so ME faces the other way

blocks.note: the indefinite article in its other form
an ad is a brief advertisement

annotation.surface: Someone pins a brief notice around a funeral wreath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Placed around' reads like a container instruction, but nothing goes inside anything: the setter's pronoun is simply turned round and added at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare, poetic word for a garland worn on the head, the kind of wreath found in old verse.

entries.clue: Rob and Peter dead drunk (9)

indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk staggers all over the place, and so do these letters

annotation.surface: Rob and Peter are out cold after a night drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rob' sits beside Peter as another man's name, but it is the verb to steal.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: to plunder or lay waste, which is robbing on a grand scale.

entries.clue: What involves four bishops in church with English saints (5)

blocks.note: S = saint, doubled for the plural

annotation.surface: A gathering of four bishops in a church dedicated to English saints.
annotation.walkthrough: The bishops look clerical, and the church and saints keep that up, but they are pieces on a board.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by a distinctive detail: each side in the game has two bishops, four in all.

entries.clue: A king intervening in quarrel? That’s a duty (6)

indicatorNotes.intervening in: to intervene is to come between, so these letters come between others

blocks.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
A plus R, from Latin rex

annotation.surface: A monarch steps into a row, and someone calls that his duty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duty' reads as a king's obligation to keep the peace, but it is a tax.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the customs sense: a tariff is a duty charged on goods.

entries.clue: African city cricket club captured by a famous artist? (5)

indicatorNotes.captured by: a captive is held inside, so these letters sit within the ones that capture them

blocks.note: A plus RA, a Royal Academician

annotation.surface: A great painter seizes a cricket club in an African city.
annotation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts, which is why a famous artist gives two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Accra is the capital of Ghana.

entries.clue: Complains, given this wasting time is out of order (8)

indicatorNotes.wasting: wasting something is losing it, so the letter is lost
indicatorNotes.is out of order: letters out of order are not in their usual sequence

blocks.note: T = time, removed to leave GIVENHIS

annotation.surface: Someone grumbles that wasting time like this is out of order.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a complaint about time-wasting; the definition sits at the front in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to inveigh is to complain loudly and bitterly, usually 'against' something.

entries.clue: Hunters over a long period north and south of river (8)

indicatorNotes.north and south of: in a down clue north is above and south is below, so the letters sit on both sides

blocks.note: for ages = for a long time

annotation.surface: Hunters have roamed for ages on both banks of a river.
annotation.walkthrough: Compass words in a down clue mean position on the page, not geography.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: foragers search the land for food, hunting it out.

entries.clue: Absolutely unfashionable? Correct! (8)

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing is utterly passé and gets the answer 'Correct!'
annotation.walkthrough: 'Absolutely' seems to intensify 'unfashionable', but it stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adverb synonym, as in 'rejected outright'.

entries.clue: Object lesson no longer enough (7)

annotation.surface: A teaching lesson that has stopped being adequate.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a verdict on a lesson; the first two words are the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a practical illustration, the sense in 'made an example of'.

entries.clue: Expose a French maiden, maybe outside front of castle (7)

indicatorNotes.outside: one piece stands outside another, wrapped round it
indicatorNotes.front of: the front of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a maiden is one kind of over in cricket

annotation.surface: A French maiden is revealed outside a castle, as in a fairy tale.
annotation.walkthrough: The maiden looks like a damsel, but in cricket a maiden is an over from which no runs are scored; 'maybe' flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to uncover a plot is to expose it.

entries.clue: Nothing wrong with you no longer guarding energy plant (5)

indicatorNotes.no longer: a word no longer in use is archaic, and YE is the archaic form of you
indicatorNotes.guarding: a guard surrounds what it protects

blocks.note: E = energy, placed between X and YE

annotation.surface: You no longer protect an energy plant, and nothing is amiss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Energy plant' reads as a power station; the plant is a flower and energy is a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the oxeye daisy is a common wild flower.

entries.clue: Celebrate, embracing what’s best, yelling (9)

indicatorNotes.embracing: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it
the cream is the best part

annotation.surface: A crowd celebrates the finest, shouting as it goes.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end, after a comma that makes it look like part of the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: screaming is yelling at its loudest.

entries.clue: “Skill needed in firm” — good criticism by the female who makes plans? (12)

indicatorNotes.needed in: something needed in a place has to go inside it
indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so the pieces follow on

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for 'one who makes plans'
annotation.surface: A job advert asks for skill and draws sharp comment on the woman who plans things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plans' suggests schemes and plotting, but a plan is also a drawn map; the quoted phrase is dressed up as a job advert.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic stretch: a plan can be a drawing of an area, and a map-maker draws them.

entries.clue: Drunk, keeping out of control mostly in declining years (8)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, here inside
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of a word is all but its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone who is drunk and wild in old age.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of control' looks like an anagram signal but is simply a synonym, shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the twilight of one's life is its final, declining stretch.

entries.clue: Bring fragrance to some tiara with new configuration (9)

indicatorNotes.with new configuration: a new configuration is a new arrangement of the same parts

annotation.surface: Someone scents a tiara that has been redesigned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a hidden-word signal but is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb is built from aroma, a fragrance, so it means give something a scent.

entries.clue: Shrill sound outside hospital able to deal with every situation (5-3)

annotation.definition: able to deal with every situation

indicatorNotes.outside: one piece stands outside another, wrapped round it

blocks.note: a catcall is a shrill whistle of disapproval

annotation.surface: A siren wails outside a hospital that copes with anything.
annotation.walkthrough: The shrill sound near a hospital suggests a siren, but the sound is a jeer.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a catch-all clause, meaning one that covers every case.

entries.clue: Against work, projecting a false image? (8)

annotation.surface: Someone who dislikes work and is putting on an act.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Against work' reads as a lazy attitude; the first word alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be opposing a plan is to be against it.

entries.clue: Gratitude for what successful investment brings financially? (12)

blocks.note: the financial sense: a rise in value

annotation.surface: Thanks offered for the rewards of a good investment.
annotation.walkthrough: The same word means thanks and, in finance, an increase in value; the 'for' makes one read as the reason for the other.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: grateful recognition, and the growth in an asset's worth.

entries.clue: Merry function welcomed by American bloke (6)

indicatorNotes.welcomed by: a guest welcomed in goes inside the host

annotation.surface: A cheerful party is hosted by an American man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a party, but it is the maths function.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: jocose means playful and jolly.

entries.clue: An ordeal restricting driver, ultimately not moving (2,4)

indicatorNotes.restricting: to restrict is to hem in, so these letters close round another
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the word's last letter

annotation.surface: A driver is put through a gruelling test while stuck in place.
annotation.walkthrough: The split is in an unexpected place: the article stays attached, and the letter lands after its T.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something at rest is stationary.

entries.clue: Choose to hold end of this when tucking into duck? (9)

annotation.definition: Choose to hold end of this when tucking into duck?

indicatorNotes.to hold: to hold something is to have it within, so one piece takes another inside
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.tucking into: tucking into is going inside, so this group goes into the next word

blocks.note: a young duck is a chick
last letter of this, inside OPT

annotation.surface: Advice to grip the end of your utensil when eating duck.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: you grip this implement by its end when tucking into Peking duck. 'Tucking into' is both eating and the container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the whole clue describes using the implement to eat duck.

entries.clue: Building illegally occupied most of courtyard in street (5)

indicatorNotes.most of: most of a word is all but its last letter
indicatorNotes.in: one piece sits in another, inside it

blocks.note: a quad is a courtyard, as in a college quadrangle

annotation.surface: Squatters move into part of a courtyard off a street.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs to three words; 'occupied' belongs to it, not to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A British noun sense: a squat is a building taken over by squatters, people living there without permission.

entries.clue: Central feature of breakfast when hot — answer? (5)

annotation.definition: Central feature of breakfast when hot — answer?

indicatorNotes.Central feature of: the central feature of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: the middle of the nine letters of breakfast

annotation.surface: Someone asks what the main part of a hot breakfast is.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the dish, a hot porridge at the heart of breakfast in Eastern Europe and Russia.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: kasha, a buckwheat porridge, really is the centrepiece of a hot breakfast.

entries.clue: Behind, having secured goalless draw abroad (5)

indicatorNotes.having secured: to secure something is to hold it fast, here inside

annotation.surface: A team trailing but holding on for a 0-0 draw away from home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' looks like the away match, but it means astir or going about, as in 'rumours abroad'.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense of abroad, out and about or in circulation, is the same as afoot.

entries.clue: Extreme characters and I articulate loveless feature of star’s position (7)

indicatorNotes.Extreme: the extreme characters of the alphabet are those at its two ends
indicatorNotes.loveless: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so loveless drops it

blocks.note: first and last letters of the alphabet
to mouth is to articulate words

annotation.surface: Someone declares that even the extremes of their words lack love for a star.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity; it is a star in the sky, and the definition belongs to astronomy.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical term: azimuth is a star's bearing round the horizon, one of the two coordinates fixing its position.

entries.clue: Feature of winter holidays only providing shelter for sleep (3,4)

indicatorNotes.providing shelter for: a shelter goes round what it protects

blocks.note: kip is British slang for sleep

annotation.surface: Winter breaks where the only draw is somewhere to sleep.
annotation.walkthrough: The break falls after the first letter, which hides the familiar word inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by association: ski poles are standard kit on a winter skiing holiday.

entries.clue: Smooth group of stars welcoming most of the spectators (6)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside another
indicatorNotes.most of: most of a word is all but its last letter

blocks.note: the gate is the attendance at a sports match

annotation.surface: A polished band of celebrities greets most of the audience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities, but the group is a constellation.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical term: legato marks notes to be played smoothly, with no gaps.

entries.clue: Returning sailor joining group with chaps hiding in lowly accommodation? (8)

indicatorNotes.Returning: something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.joining: joining puts one piece next to the other
indicatorNotes.hiding in: something hiding in a place is inside it

annotation.surface: A sailor comes home to join a gang of men holed up in cheap lodgings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lowly' is the joke: it seems to mean humble, but this accommodation is lowly because it is the lowest floor.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a basement flat is literally the lowest place to live.
